concepts.name: 08-softened-compact
concepts.description: Subtle rounding at all four tips, preserving the original taper.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Edit target: the attached Flight Deck "04 Compact Updraft" logo. The user likes this exact logo and asks for softer, more rounded pointed areas while keeping its aerodynamic character.
Preserve: its compact rising two-ribbon silhouette, two staggered upper-right terminals, curved white airflow channel, rounded lower-left banking turn, small inward/upward hooked lower tail, black-on-white palette, square presentation, symbol placement and scale, and the centered wordmark "Flight Deck" in the same bold sans serif.
Change ONLY the symbol's contour treatment as described below. This is a close design refinement, not a new logo concept. Preserve exactly two black components. Keep the white channel open and clearly legible.
Crucial: the source has four conspicuous acute points: the uppermost upper-right tip, the second upper-right tip, the bottom-left endpoint of the upper ribbon, and the small tip of the lower curl at right. Soften these deliberately. Round the actual silhouette; do NOT simulate softness with blur, glow, gradients, or shadows. Keep edges crisp, pure black, flat vector-like. Use smoothly tangent curved transitions and tapered forms ending in deliberate rounded noses. No pointed needles at those four locations.
Do not add extra ribbons, outlines, circles, decorative dots, feathers, a literal airplane, new text, or a different font. White background, no texture, no 3D. One finished logo and wordmark only.
Variation A: SUBTLE SOFTENING. Preserve the original contour as closely as possible. Replace each of the four sharp terminals with a small but clearly visible smooth convex radius. At a symbol width of 650 pixels, the visible end caps should be about 12–18 pixels across, not single-pixel points. The upper-right tips remain slender and swept, but end in neat rounded noses. Gently round the left ribbon endpoint and the small lower curl endpoint by the same visual amount. Keep the original inward lower curl shape. This should feel like the exact original refined with carefully radiused corners, taut, fast, and approachable.

concepts.name: 09-rounded-airfoil
concepts.description: Fuller rounded tips with a smooth airfoil profile.
concepts.prompt:

Do not add extra ribbons, outlines, circles, decorative dots, feathers, a literal airplane, new text, or a different font. White background, no texture, no 3D. One finished logo and wordmark only.
Variation B: ROUNDED AIRFOIL. Give all four endpoints a more substantial rounded treatment than subtle corner rounding. Shorten the needle-like upper-right ends slightly and finish them with elegant smooth asymmetric oval noses, angled along the direction of travel. A tip should remain about one fifth of the ribbon's maximum thickness before it rounds over, like a sculpted aircraft wingtip rather than a sharp blade. Round the upper ribbon's left endpoint into a soft shoulder. Give the lower hooked tail a gently rounded rising end. Preserve the long flowing taper leading into each end and the original compact silhouette and white channel. The result should feel like precise molded aerodynamic surfaces, soft but still swift, not thick sausages or bubbles.

concepts.name: 10-soft-bank
concepts.description: A gentler lower curl and softly rounded swept tips.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Edit target: the attached Flight Deck "04 Compact Updraft" logo. The user likes this exact logo and asks for softer, more rounded pointed areas while keeping its aerodynamic character.
Preserve: its compact rising two-ribbon silhouette, two staggered upper-right terminals, curved white airflow channel, rounded lower-left banking turn, small inward/upward hooked lower tail, black-on-white palette, square presentation, symbol placement and scale, and the centered wordmark "Flight Deck" in the same bold sans serif.

Variation C: SOFT BANK. Preserve the original two-ribbon rising sweep but especially refine the aggressive little hooked lower tail: open its inner concave curve slightly and turn its pointed end into a smooth rounded returning tip, like a gently banked wing. Shorten that curled tip modestly so it does not read as a claw, and make the base feel calm and continuous. Use medium visible rounding on the two ascending upper-right tips and a broad rounded termination at the lower-left endpoint of the upper ribbon. Keep the ascending tips offset and the white S-shaped channel open. All transitions must feel continuous and sculpted. Preserve speed through the upward diagonal sweep and slender tapering; introduce softness through the end radii and more relaxed lower curl. Do not enlarge the symbol or change the wordmark.
